<strong>Resistencia a colisiones</strong: Collision resistance: no pair $m_1 \ne m_2$ with the same fingerprint can be found, choosing both freely. It is the most demanding, and the one that falls first.
<strong>Resistencia a la preimagen</stro: Preimage resistance: given a hash $h$, no message $m$ with $H(m) = h$ can be found. The fingerprint cannot be undone.

Ralph Merkle propuso las funciones hash: Ralph Merkle proposed cryptographic hash functions in his 1979 thesis, and Ivan Damgård proved the construction in 1989. Ron Rivest designed MD4 and MD5 (1990, 1991); Xiaoyun Wang and her team found MD5 collisions in 2004 and announced an attack on SHA-1 in 2005. The practical SHA-1 collision was published by Google and Amsterdam's CWI in 2017, after $2^{63}$ operations: two different PDFs with the same fingerprint. SHA-2 was published by the NSA in 2001, and SHA-3 came out of a public contest, like AES, won in 2012 by Keccak.
SHA-256 encadena una función de compresi: SHA-256 chains a compression function over 512-bit blocks (Merkle-Damgård); MD5 and SHA-1 are broken.
SHA-256 procesa el mensaje en bloques de: SHA-256 processes the message in 512-bit blocks. It starts with a 256-bit state fixed by the standard, and for each block applies a compression function that mixes the state with the block in 64 rounds of additions, rotations and XORs, and returns a new state. The last state is the fingerprint. Beforehand the message is padded with a 1, zeros and its length in bits, so that two messages of different lengths cannot be padded the same.
